name: LoCoMo
summary: Long-horizon conversational-memory benchmark spanning QA, event summarization, and multimodal dialogue generation over very long multi-session conversations.
scale: Very long conversations averaging about 600 turns and 16K tokens, spanning up to 32 sessions.
measurement_strength: Established very-long-term conversational memory as a first-class evaluation target rather than a short-context dialogue property.
coverage_gap: Mostly measures memory about past conversation, not whether remembered experience improves future closed-loop action.

name: LongMemEval
summary: Evaluates sustained chat-assistant memory across extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention.
scale: 500 curated questions embedded in freely scalable user-assistant histories.
measurement_strength: Made update, temporal reasoning, and abstention explicit instead of collapsing long-term memory into factual recall.
coverage_gap: Still uses downstream QA over conversational histories rather than agent-environment experience or future task execution.

name: MemBench
summary: Broadens memory evaluation across factual and reflective memory, participation and observation scenarios, and effectiveness, efficiency, and capacity.
scale: Multiple memory levels and interactive scenarios with a released dataset and benchmark harness.
measurement_strength: Expanded evaluation from answer accuracy toward different memory levels, interaction roles, efficiency, and capacity.
coverage_gap: Scenario breadth still does not isolate which memory write, organization, retrieval, or update mechanism caused a result.

name: MemoryAgentBench
summary: Evaluates memory agents under incremental multi-turn interaction across retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and selective forgetting.
scale: Unified benchmark spanning multiple datasets and four core memory competencies.
measurement_strength: Shifted the object from a static long context to a memory agent that must incrementally absorb, update, use, and forget information.
coverage_gap: Many component comparisons remain sensitive to the surrounding answerer, embedding model, and memory harness.

name: BEAM
summary: Tests long-term memory on coherent conversations extending from million-token to multi-million-token horizons.
scale: 100 conversations and 2,000 validated questions, with conversations scalable up to 10M tokens.
measurement_strength: Made memory degradation with truly massive, coherent histories directly measurable.
coverage_gap: Long-context QA remains different from maintaining actionable memory during an evolving agent-environment loop.

name: StructMemEval
summary: Tests whether agents organize memory into task-appropriate structures such as ledgers, lists, and trees rather than only retrieving facts.
scale: A suite of tasks whose solutions require specific memory organizations such as transaction ledgers, to-do lists, and trees.
measurement_strength: Makes memory structure itself observable as a capability.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is narrow and can reward prompted structure selection rather than autonomous discovery of the right representation.

name: AMA-Bench
summary: Evaluates long-horizon memory over real and synthetic agent-environment trajectories rather than dialogue-only histories.
scale: Real-world agentic trajectories with expert QA plus synthetic trajectories scalable to arbitrary horizons.
measurement_strength: Moved agent memory from human-agent dialogue toward machine-generated agent-environment experience and causality.
coverage_gap: QA over stored trajectories still only indirectly measures whether memory improves later acting and planning.

name: LifeBench
summary: Evaluates long-horizon multi-source memory spanning declarative and non-declarative information such as habits and procedures.
scale: Densely connected long-horizon event simulations; released dataset and synthesis code.
measurement_strength: Expands memory beyond explicit facts to inferred habitual and procedural knowledge across heterogeneous traces.
coverage_gap: Synthetic life simulation may not capture the full ambiguity, privacy constraints, and action consequences of real personal data.

name: LongMemEval-V2
summary: Evaluates whether memory systems internalize environment-specific experience from large web-agent trajectory histories.
scale: 451 curated questions; histories up to 500 trajectories and 115M tokens.
measurement_strength: Makes accumulated environment experience and workflow knowledge a memory target, not merely user-history recall.
coverage_gap: The downstream task is still context gathering for QA rather than executing future tasks with the learned experience.

name: LifeSide
summary: Benchmarks lifelong digital companions through multi-session memory, user understanding, privacy control, and emotional-environment dynamics.
scale: 2,000 personas and 111K tasks.
measurement_strength: Connects memory to persistent user models, privacy boundaries, and emotional/environmental context.
coverage_gap: Simulated personas and environments may not faithfully reproduce real longitudinal human behavior or privacy expectations.

name: LoCoMo-Plus
summary: Evaluates cognitive memory where agents must retain and apply latent user constraints even when later cues are semantically disconnected.
scale: ACL 2026 benchmark and evaluation framework built to extend LoCoMo beyond explicit factual recall.
measurement_strength: Moves the target from remembering explicit facts to applying latent user state, goals, and values when the cue no longer restates them.
coverage_gap: Still focuses on conversational response consistency rather than embodied or tool-mediated long-horizon action.

name: HotpotQA
summary: A foundational multi-hop QA benchmark requiring evidence retrieval and reasoning across multiple supporting documents.
scale: 113K Wikipedia-based question-answer pairs with sentence-level supporting facts.
measurement_strength: Established multi-document evidence composition and explainable supporting facts as measurable retrieval-reasoning targets.
coverage_gap: Static Wikipedia QA does not test dynamic search, tool interfaces, iterative retrieval control, or real-world information drift.

name: KILT
summary: Unifies knowledge-intensive tasks against one Wikipedia snapshot and evaluates downstream task quality together with provenance.
scale: A unified suite spanning multiple knowledge-intensive task families and datasets on one shared knowledge source.
measurement_strength: Made retrieval provenance and reusable retrieval infrastructure first-class across multiple downstream tasks.
coverage_gap: A fixed shared snapshot removes freshness, interactive search, and environment/tool-state challenges central to modern agents.

name: BEIR
summary: A heterogeneous benchmark for zero-shot information retrieval generalization across diverse domains and retrieval tasks.
scale: Originally 18 retrieval datasets spanning diverse domains and tasks.
measurement_strength: Established cross-domain robustness as a retriever requirement instead of optimizing only one benchmark such as MS MARCO.
coverage_gap: Retriever-only evaluation does not measure iterative information seeking, answer generation, tool choice, or stateful search.

name: MultiHop-RAG
summary: A RAG-specific benchmark requiring retrieval and reasoning over multiple pieces of supporting evidence.
scale: A news-based knowledge base with multi-hop queries, ground-truth answers, and associated supporting evidence.
measurement_strength: Made multi-hop retrieval failure visible inside a RAG pipeline instead of treating retrieval as single-shot relevance.
coverage_gap: Static corpus and fixed pipeline do not test adaptive search, live web state, or tool-mediated retrieval.

name: CRAG
summary: A factual RAG benchmark spanning dynamic facts, long-tail entities, web search, and knowledge-graph retrieval.
scale: 4,409 question-answer pairs across five domains and eight question categories.
measurement_strength: Made freshness, popularity, and factual dynamism central to RAG evaluation and powered the KDD Cup 2024 challenge.
coverage_gap: Mock retrieval APIs do not reproduce all control-flow and interface complexity of live information-seeking agents.

name: RAGBench
summary: A large-scale labeled benchmark for explainable evaluation of RAG systems across industry-oriented domains.
scale: 100K examples spanning five industry-specific domains and multiple RAG task types.
measurement_strength: Shifted attention from only benchmarking RAG systems to benchmarking the evaluators and actionable failure labels used to judge them.
coverage_gap: Evaluation-label quality is not the same as measuring adaptive retrieval policy or agentic information seeking.

name: BrowseComp
summary: Benchmarks browsing agents on hard-to-find questions that require persistent web navigation and creative information seeking.
scale: 1,266 browsing questions with short verifiable answers.
measurement_strength: Made persistence and creativity in web information seeking a simple, widely reusable agent benchmark.
coverage_gap: Short-answer tasks omit long-form synthesis, ambiguity resolution, citation quality, and realistic user-query distributions.

name: DeepResearch Bench
summary: Evaluates deep-research agents on multi-step web research, evidence collection, citation quality, and long-form report synthesis.
scale: 100 PhD-level research tasks across 22 fields.
measurement_strength: Expanded search-agent evaluation from finding an answer to producing analyst-style, citation-rich research artifacts.
coverage_gap: Only 100 high-cost tasks and evaluator dependence make fine-grained causal attribution difficult.

name: RAGCap-Bench
summary: Decomposes agentic RAG into intermediate capabilities and evaluates those capabilities independently of final-answer quality.
scale: A targeted capability suite derived from recurring tasks and failure patterns in agentic RAG systems.
measurement_strength: Made intermediate agentic-RAG skills an explicit evaluation object rather than attributing end-to-end failures to a black box.
coverage_gap: Capability scores matter only if they predict realized end-to-end behavior under matched tools and resource budgets.

name: AgenticRAGTracer
summary: Diagnoses multi-step agentic RAG by providing hop-aware intermediate validation rather than only final questions and answers.
scale: 1,305 benchmark instances spanning multiple domains.
measurement_strength: Makes where a retrieval-reasoning chain fails observable at hop granularity.
coverage_gap: Automatically generated hop structure may reflect benchmark construction artifacts rather than causal agent steps.

name: SGR-Bench
summary: Benchmarks search agents when answer-bearing evidence appears only after the agent establishes the correct site-specific retrieval state.
scale: 100 expert-curated tasks across six source families and 12 public data ecosystems.
measurement_strength: Separates finding the right source from configuring the right filters, hierarchy, scope, or view inside that source.
coverage_gap: State-gated retrieval is important but narrower than general web research, document RAG, or arbitrary tool orchestration.

name: VAKRA
summary: Evaluates agents that must compose executable APIs, document retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, and natural-language tool-use policies.
scale: Over 8,000 executable APIs across 62 domains with single-hop, compositional, and multi-source tasks.
measurement_strength: Unifies structured API interaction and unstructured retrieval in one executable evaluation with policy constraints.
coverage_gap: A fixed ReAct harness isolates model capability but does not measure the quality of alternative agent architectures.

name: WikiSQL
summary: A large early benchmark for translating natural-language questions into executable SQL over individual Wikipedia tables.
scale: 80,654 human-annotated question-SQL examples across 24,241 tables.
measurement_strength: Made executable natural-language database querying a large-scale benchmarkable task.
coverage_gap: Single-table SQL omits schema discovery, joins, heterogeneous sources, multi-step analysis, and tool orchestration.

name: Spider
summary: A foundational cross-domain text-to-SQL benchmark requiring generalization to unseen database schemas and complex multi-table SQL.
scale: 10,181 questions, 5,693 unique SQL queries, and 200 databases across 138 domains.
measurement_strength: Made cross-schema generalization and complex SQL the canonical database-language benchmark rather than memorizing one schema.
coverage_gap: Static text-to-SQL still abstracts away metadata search, business logic, multi-step workflows, and heterogeneous data.

name: DS-1000
summary: A natural benchmark for data-science code generation across major Python data libraries with execution-grounded evaluation.
scale: 1,000 data-science problems spanning seven Python libraries.
measurement_strength: Established reliable executable evaluation for practical data-science coding beyond SQL.
coverage_gap: Single-code-generation problems do not capture end-to-end analysis, iterative exploration, or multi-tool agent workflows.

name: BIRD
summary: A large database-grounded text-to-SQL benchmark emphasizing real database values, dirty content, external knowledge, and SQL efficiency.
scale: 12,751 text-to-SQL pairs over 95 databases totaling 33.4 GB across 37 domains.
measurement_strength: Moved text-to-SQL toward large, messy, value-rich databases and made SQL efficiency visible.
coverage_gap: The interaction remains query-centric rather than a full enterprise data workflow with multiple tools and data systems.

name: Spider 2.0
summary: Evaluates language models on realistic enterprise text-to-SQL workflows involving huge schemas, multiple SQL dialects, metadata, codebases, and cloud databases.
scale: 632 real-world enterprise text-to-SQL workflow problems, often over databases with more than 1,000 columns.
measurement_strength: Turned text-to-SQL from a one-shot semantic parsing task into a long-horizon enterprise workflow problem.
coverage_gap: Still centers SQL workflows rather than heterogeneous documents, multimedia, reporting, or broader data-science lifecycle tasks.

name: DataSciBench
summary: Benchmarks LLM agents on diverse data-science tasks with programmatic Task-Function-Code evaluation and human-verified ground truth.
scale: A curated benchmark of natural data-science prompts evaluated across many API and open-source models.
measurement_strength: Broadened evaluation beyond easily graded single tasks toward heterogeneous data-science prompts and task-specific metrics.
coverage_gap: Does not fully reproduce operating-system-level, multi-application, end-to-end data-science work.

name: FDABench
summary: Evaluates data agents on analytical queries over heterogeneous structured, unstructured, web, and multimodal data.
scale: 2,007 tasks across 50+ domains, three task types, and heterogeneous data sources.
measurement_strength: Expanded data-agent evaluation from SQL or code to multi-source analytical workflows, while exposing cost and reasoning traces.
coverage_gap: Large task diversity does not itself isolate which planning, retrieval, semantic, or execution component caused success.

name: Data Agent Benchmark (DAB)
summary: Evaluates enterprise data agents on questions requiring integration, transformation, and analysis across multiple heterogeneous database systems.
scale: 54 queries across 12 datasets, 9 domains, and 4 database management systems.
measurement_strength: Targets the full enterprise data-question pipeline rather than isolated SQL generation or small in-context tables.
coverage_gap: A relatively small task set and system-level harness differences limit fine-grained component attribution.

name: AgenticDataBench
summary: Benchmarks data agents across realistic data-science workflows using a skill taxonomy to quantify fine-grained coverage.
scale: Tasks from 15 vertical domains including five real-world B2B use cases, plus skill-driven generated coverage.
measurement_strength: Makes data-science skill coverage itself explicit, enabling diagnosis beyond aggregate task success.
coverage_gap: Skill taxonomies and generated tasks may not capture organization-specific semantics, evolving data, or governance constraints.

name: DataSpace
summary: Evaluates verifiable analytics over heterogeneous workspaces where evidence spans databases, files, documents, and multimedia.
scale: 410 tasks over 7,439 artifacts totaling 15.01 GB; official KDD Cup 2026 data-agent benchmark.
measurement_strength: Unifies heterogeneous evidence discovery with deterministic complete-result evaluation in a task-local workspace.
coverage_gap: Task-local workspaces still avoid longitudinal enterprise change, permissions, writes, and collaborative data operations.

name: DSAgentBench
summary: Evaluates agents on complete data-science workflows inside real computer environments using notebooks, IDEs, terminals, browsers, and databases.
scale: 275 tasks spanning the full data-science lifecycle.
measurement_strength: Moves data-agent evaluation into real computer environments where success requires multi-stage, multi-tool execution grounded in intermediate outputs.
coverage_gap: Real-computer execution increases realism but also makes results sensitive to environment setup and tool/harness implementation.

name: Beyond Goldfish Memory
summary: Benchmarks long-term open-domain conversation across multiple human-human chat sessions where partners must remember and remain consistent with prior interactions.
scale: A released human-human dataset of conversations resumed across multiple chat sessions.
measurement_strength: Established cross-session conversation as a distinct long-term-memory setting before modern memory-agent benchmarks.
coverage_gap: Conversation continuity does not test explicit memory writing, updates, tool use, or future environment actions.

name: Mem-Gallery
summary: Evaluates multimodal long-term conversational memory across extraction and test-time adaptation, reasoning, and memory knowledge management.
scale: High-quality multi-session visual-text conversations with a unified framework benchmarked across 12 memory systems.
measurement_strength: Makes visual retention, multimodal reasoning, and memory organization first-class long-term-memory evaluation targets.
coverage_gap: Conversational readout still leaves action utility indirect and comparisons remain sensitive to the multimodal backbone and surrounding harness.

name: MemoryArena
summary: Evaluates memory inside multi-session Memory-Agent-Environment loops where earlier actions and feedback must be distilled and used to guide later actions.
scale: Five task and environment families spanning shopping, search, travel planning, mathematics, and physics.
measurement_strength: Directly couples long-term memorization with future action instead of evaluating recall and acting as separate abilities.
coverage_gap: Finite benchmark episodes still fall short of truly persistent deployments with long-lived state, permissions, irreversible actions, and recovery.

name: MemEye
summary: Benchmarks visual-centric agent memory across fine-grained visual evidence and temporal visual-state synthesis while checking whether visual evidence is genuinely necessary.
scale: 371 mirrored multiple-choice and open-ended questions across 8 life-scenario tasks.
measurement_strength: Forces systems to retain genuinely necessary visual evidence rather than succeeding through text-only shortcuts or coarse captions.
coverage_gap: Constructed scenarios and judge-based open-ended scoring do not establish long-horizon action utility in real multimodal environments.

name: RealMem
summary: Evaluates long-term memory over project-oriented cross-session interactions whose goals, artifacts, and relevant state evolve over time.
scale: More than 2,000 cross-session dialogues across 11 realistic project scenarios.
measurement_strength: Moves long-term-memory evaluation from casual conversation toward persistent project state and evolving user goals.
coverage_gap: Synthetic multi-agent trajectory generation and dialogue-only interaction still abstract away real collaborative writes, permissions, and tooling.

name: Mem2ActBench
summary: Evaluates whether long-term memory is proactively used for tool selection and parameter grounding during tool-based assistant actions.
scale: 400 tool-use tasks generated from 2,029 sessions averaging 12 user-assistant-tool turns; 91.3% were judged strongly memory-dependent.
measurement_strength: Makes action-level memory utilization directly measurable instead of reading memory quality only through answers about past context.
coverage_gap: Tool-call tasks remain narrower than long-horizon environments where actions alter persistent state and mistakes have downstream consequences.

name: RGB
summary: Decomposes retrieval-augmented generation into noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.
scale: Four English and Chinese diagnostic testbeds covering four distinct RAG abilities.
measurement_strength: Made correct use of retrieved context a multi-dimensional evaluation target rather than a single end-to-end answer score.
coverage_gap: Static supplied contexts do not measure retriever quality, iterative search control, or live information environments.

name: RAGTruth
summary: Provides fine-grained manual annotations of hallucinations in naturally generated RAG responses for evaluating grounding and hallucination detection.
scale: Nearly 18,000 naturally generated RAG responses with manual annotations at case and word level.
measurement_strength: Makes localized grounding failures in RAG outputs measurable instead of reducing faithfulness to one document- or answer-level label.
coverage_gap: It evaluates generated outputs and detectors rather than adaptive retrieval policy or end-to-end search behavior.

name: BRIGHT
summary: Benchmarks retrieval on real-world queries where identifying relevant documents itself requires substantial reasoning.
scale: 1,384 real-world queries across domains including economics, psychology, mathematics, and coding.
measurement_strength: Shows that semantic similarity alone under-tests retrieval when relevance depends on reasoning about the query and candidate documents.
coverage_gap: Static retriever evaluation does not test iterative agentic search, evidence-portfolio construction, or tool-state control.

name: BrowseComp-Plus
summary: Recasts deep-research evaluation over a fixed, curated corpus to isolate retriever and agent contributions and improve fairness and reproducibility.
scale: 830 queries over roughly 100,000 fixed human-verified documents with verified positives and hard negatives.
measurement_strength: Makes BrowseComp-style deep research reproducible enough to attribute gains to retrieval and agent behavior rather than an opaque live search stack.
coverage_gap: A fixed corpus improves control but removes freshness, provider variation, and much of the interface complexity of the live web.

name: MLAgentBench
summary: Benchmarks agents that iteratively design, execute, inspect, and improve machine-learning experiments rather than merely generating code once.
scale: 13 machine-learning experimentation tasks ranging from established datasets to recent research challenges.
measurement_strength: Turns data-science coding into an iterative scientific-experimentation problem with feedback from executed results.
coverage_gap: A small task set and fixed experimentation environments do not represent the breadth of enterprise data work or long-lived projects.

name: InsightBench
summary: Evaluates end-to-end business analytics from question formulation through insight extraction and actionable recommendations.
scale: 100 business-use-case datasets with curated planted insights.
measurement_strength: Moves data-agent evaluation from answering a given query toward discovering and communicating useful analysis.
coverage_gap: Planted insights and evaluator-based scoring constrain how well the benchmark captures genuinely open-ended discovery or causal business value.

name: DA-Code
summary: Evaluates grounded executable data-analysis code over diverse real data, spanning wrangling, exploratory analysis, and machine learning.
scale: 500 tasks across Data Wrangling, Machine Learning, and Exploratory Data Analysis.
measurement_strength: Bridges static code generation and agent-style data work by requiring planning and executable grounding in task data.
coverage_gap: The target remains code and task output rather than full enterprise discovery, reporting, governance, or multi-application workflows.

name: DAComp
summary: Benchmarks both repository-level data engineering and open-ended data analysis to cover a broader data-intelligence lifecycle.
scale: 210 tasks spanning data engineering and open-ended data analysis.
measurement_strength: Separates and jointly covers data engineering and analysis, moving evaluation toward the full data-intelligence lifecycle rather than isolated query or code tasks.
coverage_gap: Open-ended analysis remains judge-sensitive, while repository and runtime setup can materially affect system-level comparisons.

name: ImplicitMemBench
summary: Evaluates whether learned procedures, priming, and conditioned associations automatically alter an agent's first behavior without an explicit recall request.
scale: 300 items evenly divided across procedural memory, priming, and classical conditioning, spanning 18 task families.
measurement_strength: Makes automatic behavioral enactment after experience observable instead of inferring memory only from explicit factual recall.
coverage_gap: Short in-context episodes do not establish durable cross-session memory, external-store updating, forgetting, or action in a persistent environment.

name: MemEvoBench
summary: Evaluates safety degradation as misleading memories, noisy tool outputs, and biased feedback accumulate through repeated memory updates.
scale: 108 QA cases across 7 domains and 36 risk types, plus 83 workflow cases adapted from 20 Agent-SafetyBench environments.
measurement_strength: Makes gradual unsafe behavioral drift over successive memory writes measurable rather than treating each unsafe response as an isolated failure.
coverage_gap: It does not connect each poisoned write to an externally verified consequence and selective repair, or test authorization in shared memory.

name: MEMPROBE
summary: Audits the final memory artifact left after ordinary assistance by reconstructing a simulated user's hidden structured state.
scale: 50 simulated users with 31 hidden dimensions each, yielding 1,550 recovery targets across five user-state categories.
measurement_strength: Directly measures what structured user state survives in the memory artifact and separates stored information from top-k accessibility.
coverage_gap: Recoverability can reward unnecessary profiling and does not establish downstream usefulness, consent, privacy compliance, deletion, or action quality.

name: GateMem
summary: Evaluates whether a shared-memory agent remains useful while enforcing contextual access boundaries and honoring deletion requests across multiple principals.
scale: 91 long-form multi-party episodes and 2,218 hidden checkpoints across medical, office, education, and household settings.
measurement_strength: Jointly exposes legitimate utility, unauthorized disclosure, and post-deletion recovery in a common shared-memory protocol.
coverage_gap: Behavioral non-retrieval does not prove physical erasure, and synthetic identities and policies do not test real authentication or access infrastructure.

name: CAME-Bench
summary: Evaluates context-aware retrieval when recurring entities and facts belong to different latent goals in long, interleaved trajectories.
scale: 14 trajectories and 373 questions across travel planning and debate, with average contexts of about 23K, 137K, and 408K tokens.
measurement_strength: Makes retrieval errors caused by recurring entities under incompatible latent goals directly observable.
coverage_gap: The benchmark remains synthetic retrieval and QA without real users, persistent actions, security boundaries, or memory repair.

name: MEMLENS
summary: Compares long-context vision-language models and memory-augmented agents on multimodal multi-session memory under controlled context lengths.
scale: 789 questions over four context lengths from 32K to 256K tokens and 4,695 unique images; memory agents use a fixed 195-question subset.
measurement_strength: Separates the length degradation of native long-context models from visual-fidelity loss introduced by external-memory compression.
coverage_gap: Multimodal conversation QA does not test environment actions or cleanly localize failures among writing, compression, retrieval, and answering.

name: PerMemSafe
summary: Evaluates whether evolving user memory makes an agent recognize implicit personalized risks and correctly track when those risks change or resolve.
scale: 276 user-assistant conversations yielding 750 test instances across five safety-risk domains, with irrelevant exchanges exceeding 90% of each history.
measurement_strength: Makes context-dependent safety measurable when a query is benign alone but unsafe given implicit and evolving user history.
coverage_gap: It does not test real users, tool-mediated consequences, access control, deletion, or adversarial memory poisoning.

name: MemGUI-Bench
summary: Evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse through executable mobile GUI tasks spanning steps, applications, and repeated attempts.
scale: 128 tasks in 64 mirror pairs across 26 applications and 68 scenarios; 89.8% require cross-temporal and cross-spatial retention.
measurement_strength: Directly measures whether retained information and prior execution experience improve later mobile actions and failure recovery.
coverage_gap: Snapshot-based mobile tasks do not represent indefinitely persistent user memory, permissions, or irreversible long-term consequences.

name: MedMemoryBench
summary: Evaluates streaming accumulation, clinical-state tracking, and memory saturation over long synthetic patient-assistant histories.
scale: 20 longitudinal patient personas, about 2,020 sessions, 16,000 turns, and 1,986 evaluation queries in Chinese and English.
measurement_strength: Makes performance degradation under continuing clinical information influx observable through a streaming rather than static evaluation protocol.
coverage_gap: Synthetic dialogues and QA do not establish clinical deployment safety, real patient validity, tool use, or downstream health outcomes.

name: GroupMemBench
summary: Evaluates memory in multi-party conversations where answers depend on speaker-grounded beliefs, group dynamics, and audience-specific language.
scale: Four synthetic enterprise domains with 745 released questions across multi-hop, update, temporal, user-implicit, ambiguity, and abstention categories.
measurement_strength: Makes participant identity, reply structure, group state, and audience-dependent terminology first-class memory variables.
coverage_gap: Synthetic enterprise channels do not test real organizational permissions, deletion, collaborative writes, or external actions.

name: WorldMemArena
summary: Evaluates multimodal memory over evolving action-world trajectories while separately inspecting writing, maintenance, retrieval, and use.
scale: The current artifact contains 461 samples with a balanced 150-sample subset; the paper describes 400 annotated multi-session multimodal tasks.
measurement_strength: Localizes failures to memory writing, maintenance, retrieval, or use instead of collapsing the full lifecycle into final answer accuracy.
coverage_gap: Constructed trajectories and checkpoint QA still fall short of long-lived environments with irreversible future actions, permissions, and recovery.

name: DynamicMem
summary: Evaluates whether personal-assistant memory infers and updates attributes, habits, and preferences from months of distributed multi-application behavior.
scale: Fifteen months per user, averaging 2.2M tokens and 1,772 grounded events across 16 applications, evaluated at five quarterly checkpoints.
measurement_strength: Separately measures reconstruction of an evolving user profile and its use in personalized service as histories grow to multi-million-token scale.
coverage_gap: Synthetic app traces do not reproduce real consent, privacy, permissions, unmodeled behavior, or the consequences of acting on an incorrect profile.

name: InMind
summary: Tests whether an agent retrieves a personal fact when its relevance to a later query is mediated by world knowledge rather than semantic similarity.
scale: 125 expert-verified English tasks across 10 life domains; 113 tasks are grounded in cited public sources.
measurement_strength: Paired controls separate storage failure, missing backbone knowledge, retrieval-routing failure, and final application failure.
coverage_gap: Each task centers on one synthetic personal fact in a fixed text history and does not test updating, forgetting, actions, or shared-memory governance.

name: EvoMemBench
summary: Standardizes memory-system comparison across in-episode and cross-episode scope and across knowledge-oriented and execution-oriented content.
scale: 5,754 samples across six released settings covering the four scope-by-content cells, with 15 representative memory methods compared in the paper.
measurement_strength: Places knowledge and execution memory within one in-episode versus cross-episode coordinate system under a common comparison protocol.
coverage_gap: The suite aggregates heterogeneous source benchmarks and does not provide one controlled environment in which all four memory forms are directly matched.

name: KramaBench
summary: Evaluates end-to-end data-to-insight pipelines that must discover, clean, integrate, analyze, and model messy heterogeneous data-lake files.
scale: 104 tasks decomposed into 633 subtasks over 1,764 files (1.7 GB), 24 data sources, and 6 domains.
measurement_strength: Makes both whole-lake evidence discovery and the design and implementation of intermediate pipeline functionality observable.
coverage_gap: Static offline file lakes do not test permissions, writes, longitudinal enterprise change, collaboration, or multi-application workflows.

name: DABstep
summary: Evaluates realistic multi-step financial-data analysis that combines code-based processing with contextual reasoning over transaction data and heterogeneous documentation.
scale: The paper release contains 450 tasks generated from 95 core workflows over more than 100K transactions; the current public dataset exposes 460 rows.
measurement_strength: Objective factoid checks expose whether an agent can carry domain rules through a long chain of documentation-grounded data operations.
coverage_gap: One payments domain and factoid outputs leave visualization, open reports, user interaction, and real database lifecycle work uncovered.

name: DataClawBench
summary: Evaluates exploratory financial analysis when agents receive little prior guidance and must find, understand, and reason across unfamiliar noisy data before producing verifiable conclusions.
scale: 492 tasks across 7 categories and 2-9 gold milestones, grounded in about 2.06M real records from enterprise, industry, and policy sources with native noise retained.
measurement_strength: Milestone scoring separates relevant exploratory progress from aimless tool activity and final-answer failure.
coverage_gap: The financial-consulting setting is geographically and temporally concentrated and does not cover broader multi-application enterprise operations.

name: TML-Bench
summary: Evaluates whether coding agents can reliably produce valid, competitive tabular-ML submissions under fixed wall-clock budgets and hidden labels.
scale: 4 Kaggle-style competitions, 10 open-source LLMs, 3 time budgets (240, 600, and 1,200 seconds), and 5 successful runs per task-budget setting.
measurement_strength: Jointly exposes end-to-end validity, private-holdout quality, success rate, time scaling, and run-to-run variability.
coverage_gap: Four competitions cover only tabular prediction and omit discovery, multimodal analysis, reporting, interaction, and enterprise semantics.

name: DSGym
summary: Provides a standardized, extensible execution framework and shortcut-filtered suite for evaluating and training data-science agents across analysis, prediction, and domain-specialized tasks.
scale: DSGym-Tasks contains 972 analysis and 114 prediction tasks (1,086 total); extensions include 90 DSBio tasks and DSPredict competition tasks across more than 10 domains.
measurement_strength: A common executable interface plus no-data shortcut audits make cross-suite grounding and agent behavior more comparable.
coverage_gap: Task-local containers still omit visualization-centric work, enterprise permissions, multi-application state, and longitudinal data operations.

name: DSAEval
summary: Evaluates agents on cumulative multi-query data-science projects over tabular, image, and text data, scoring reasoning, code, and results.
scale: 641 problems grounded in 285 real-world datasets, spanning structured and unstructured modalities and evaluated across 13 agents.
measurement_strength: Makes multimodal perception and cumulative project context observable alongside the quality of reasoning, executable code, and results.
coverage_gap: A notebook sandbox does not reproduce multi-application enterprise state, permissions, collaboration, or production writes.

name: LiveSQLBench
summary: Continuously evaluates SQL agents on evolving industrial databases, hierarchical knowledge, business-rule drift, and both query and management operations.
scale: Base-Lite has 270 tasks over 18 databases; Base-Full has 600 over 22; Large-v1 has 480 over 18 industrial-scale databases averaging about 1K columns and 54 tables.
measurement_strength: Fresh hidden releases, management SQL, large schemas, and knowledge-base drift make contamination, operational behavior, and adaptation visible together.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is SQL-specific and does not cover broader file, multimodal, modeling, reporting, or collaborative data-science workflows.

name: DDR-Bench
summary: Evaluates investigatory intelligence by giving an agent only an entity and database metadata, then requiring autonomous goal setting, exploration, and verifiable insight discovery.
scale: 291 entities across MIMIC (100), GLOBEM (91), and 10-K (100), covering more than 203M records, 40 tables, 6,372 fields, and 2,058 checklist items.
measurement_strength: Directly measures whether an agent can decide what is worth investigating and substantiate insights without a supplied analytical question.
coverage_gap: Three domains, restricted MIMIC access, checker dependence, and the absence of interactive stakeholders or persistent writes limit external validity.

name: DARE-bench
summary: Evaluates verifiable machine-learning modeling and instruction fidelity, including whether agents follow prescribed data-science processes rather than only obtain a plausible score.
scale: The paper defines 6,300 tasks (5,948 train and 352 evaluation); the public repository currently exposes a smaller 4,274-train and 324-evaluation subset.
measurement_strength: Objective ground truth makes both prescribed-process fidelity and predictive-model quality reproducible without an LLM judge.
coverage_gap: The suite is prediction-centered and its synthetic or LLM-assisted task formulation does not cover open-ended discovery, analysis, reporting, or production data work.

name: AgentFuel
summary: Introduces customizable end-to-end functional evaluations for conversational time-series agents, emphasizing domain-specific, stateful, and incident-specific queries.
scale: 72 released queries across 3 domains: 24 per domain, split into 12 stateless and 12 stateful or incident-specific queries, over approximately 13.5 MB of generated data.
measurement_strength: Makes domain customization and state-dependent incident reasoning explicit evaluation axes for time-series agents.
coverage_gap: The public artifact contains generated benchmark datasets and queries but not a public AgentFuel generator implementation; coverage is limited to 72 queries and 3 domains.

name: CausalDS
summary: Evaluates tool-using data-science agents on executable causal tasks across all three Pearl rungs, including identification, counterfactuals, uncertainty, and warranted abstention.
scale: 953 generated causal scenes; the reported realistic examination set contains 100 scenes or tasks spanning Rung 1 (28), Rung 2 (51), and Rung 3 (21), with clean and proxy observation variants.
measurement_strength: Makes causal identification, estimation, counterfactual reasoning, uncertainty, and abstention jointly observable in an executable data-science setting.
coverage_gap: Synthetic stories and observational data do not test live interventions, interactive experimentation, or real decision consequences.

name: WarehouseReliabilityBench
summary: Evaluates whether analytics agents return business-correct answers and appropriately clarify, abstain, or refuse under semantic ambiguity, unanswerability, schema drift, and adversarial prompts.
scale: 400 frozen tasks over 2 deterministic synthetic warehouses; 184 tasks are answerable and 216 specify clarification, abstention, or refusal behavior, with an 80-task held-out test split.
measurement_strength: Business Truth Rate and False Success Rate expose semantically wrong successful executions and correct non-answer behavior beyond SQL accuracy.
coverage_gap: Two hand-constructed synthetic warehouses and rule contracts do not establish robustness to natural enterprise conversations or diverse organizational semantics.

name: Data Exploration Benchmark
summary: Evaluates whether an agent can first construct a structured, source-grounded understanding of a complex workbook before attempting downstream analysis.
scale: Two settings: one real multi-sheet Vitamin D study workbook and 12 targeted DSBench workbook tasks (4 easy, 5 medium, and 3 difficult).
measurement_strength: Directly scores dataset understanding and experimentally measures its downstream value by comparing raw-data, self-produced exploration, and oracle-exploration conditions.
coverage_gap: The suite is small and spreadsheet-specific; optional LLM judging of the summary and oracle-artifact construction affect validity.

name: IRTS-ToolBench
summary: Evaluates tool-grounded question answering over irregularly sampled time series with asynchronous observations, informative missingness, and varying frequencies.
scale: 1,700 questions across 10 task types and 13 domains, supported by 30 tools: 7 irregularity operators and 23 analytical tools.
measurement_strength: Separates irregular-sampling reasoning and grounded tool choice from the regular-grid assumptions of prior time-series QA.
coverage_gap: Mostly constrained univariate QA with synthetically induced irregularity leaves multivariate streams and long-horizon analyst workflows uncovered.

name: StatABench
summary: Evaluates statistical knowledge, tool-grounded practical analysis, and end-to-end open statistical modeling and reporting in one suite.
scale: Stat-Closed contains 404 questions over 18 topics and 4 formats; 198 practical tasks use a 35-function toolkit; Stat-Open adds 30 modeling-competition tasks.
measurement_strength: Bridges controlled statistical knowledge and tool-use diagnostics with open end-to-end modeling reports scored for methodology, practicality, coherence, interpretation, and bias.
coverage_gap: Only 30 tasks are open-ended, and the suite does not cover data discovery, enterprise context, collaboration, or production operations.

name: AgentDS
summary: Benchmarks AI-only and human-AI collaborative performance on domain-specific predictive data-science challenges across six industries.
scale: 17 challenges across commerce, food production, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, and retail banking; the competition involved 29 teams and 80 participants.
measurement_strength: Makes domain expertise and human-AI collaboration a direct comparison axis rather than treating autonomous agent performance as the only endpoint.
coverage_gap: Synthetic datasets and prediction-centered challenges do not cover the wider analysis lifecycle, and team performance mixes agent quality with human effort and expertise.

name: Bright-Pro
summary: Evaluates reasoning-intensive retrievers with expert-annotated reasoning aspects and evidence portfolios under both static ranking and retriever-in-the-loop agentic search.
scale: 739 queries across 7 StackExchange domains, with 2,763 reasoning aspects, 5,272 gold passages, and 526,319 documents; 175 queries form the agentic-search subset.
measurement_strength: Extends BRIGHT from narrow relevance sets to weighted aspect coverage and directly measures whether a retriever supplies complementary evidence inside iterative agent workflows.
coverage_gap: Coverage is text-only and limited to seven StackExchange domains; the agentic protocol uses 175 queries and does not test live-web drift or multimodal evidence.

name: SAGE
summary: Benchmarks scientific-literature retrieval for deep-research agents on targeted paper finding and open-ended evidence collection over a controlled corpus.
scale: 1,200 expert queries across computer science, healthcare, humanities, and natural science: 600 short-form and 600 open-ended queries over a 200,000-paper corpus.
measurement_strength: Separates targeted from open-ended scientific discovery and exposes agent-retriever fit by swapping search backends under a controlled paper collection.
coverage_gap: The released repository provides query and ground-truth files but not a turnkey copy of the full 200,000-paper corpus and evaluation environment.

name: GISA
summary: Evaluates general information-seeking assistants on human-authored stable and live web queries with structured answers and complete human search trajectories.
scale: 373 human-crafted queries spanning ten topic groups, four answer formats (item, set, list, and table), stable and live subsets, and a complete human search trajectory for every query.
measurement_strength: Combines deep lookup and broad aggregation while using deterministic structured-answer scoring and human process traces instead of relying only on final-answer LLM judging.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is English, relatively small, and its live subset requires continuing answer maintenance to remain valid.

name: MTRAG-UN
summary: Tests retrieval and generation in multi-turn RAG conversations containing unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone, and unclear turns.
scale: 666 tasks from 666 conversations containing more than 2,800 turns across six domains, with accompanying retrieval corpora.
measurement_strength: Adds explicit conversational failure modes to a reusable multi-turn RAG setup and evaluates retrieval and response behavior rather than collapsing them into one score.
coverage_gap: The setting is English and corpus-bound, with no live knowledge change, multimodal evidence, or tool-choice behavior.

name: MC-Search
summary: Benchmarks multimodal agentic RAG with long, stepwise search chains annotated for subquestions, retrieval modality, supporting evidence, and intermediate answers.
scale: 3,333 tasks averaging about 3.7 hops across five reasoning topologies. The paper reports a 389,750-image and 784,473-text knowledge base; the current released dataset exposes 10,953 images and 14,037 passages.
measurement_strength: Provides hop-level planning and retrieval signals for multimodal search, making over-retrieval, under-retrieval, modality errors, and trajectory deviation observable.
coverage_gap: The corpus is limited to Wikipedia text and images and does not cover live web search, audio, video, or alternative valid reasoning trajectories.

name: LIT-RAGBench
summary: Isolates RAG generator behavior on supplied contexts covering Logic, Integration, Table, Reasoning, and Abstention capabilities in Japanese and English.
scale: 114 human-constructed Japanese questions with machine-translated, human-curated English counterparts; examples contain positive and negative chunks and can combine multiple capability labels.
measurement_strength: Controls away retriever quality so generator failures in evidence integration, logic, tables, reasoning, and abstention can be diagnosed under one protocol.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is small and does not evaluate retrieval, iterative search, citation quality, or agent policy.

name: MERRIN
summary: Evaluates search agents that must infer the needed modality, retrieve noisy or conflicting multimodal web evidence, and perform multi-hop reasoning.
scale: 162 human-annotated short-answer questions requiring evidence from images, video, audio, charts, or combinations of modalities, without explicit modality cues.
measurement_strength: Makes modality selection and evidence retrieval first-class under realistic web noise and compares no-search, native-search, and agentic-search settings.
coverage_gap: Only 162 short-answer tasks are included, and reproducibility is constrained by live-web change and proprietary search interfaces.

name: MuDABench
summary: Tests analytical question answering that requires extraction, aggregation, and quantitative reasoning across large collections of semi-structured financial documents.
scale: 332 analytical questions over more than 80,000 financial-report pages; the current repository organizes 166 simple and 166 complex questions with 589 source PDFs.
measurement_strength: Moves multi-document QA from a few supporting sources to collection-wide extraction and aggregation, with intermediate-fact coverage as a process diagnostic.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is finance-specific and relatively small; some tasks depend on document coverage and corrected annotations in the evolving release.

name: AutoResearchBench
summary: Evaluates autonomous scientific literature discovery through targeted paper finding and exhaustive set collection in a controlled full-text corpus.
scale: 1,000 queries across eight computer-science areas: 600 Deep Research tasks and 400 Wide Research tasks over a DeepXiv corpus of more than 3 million full-text papers.
measurement_strength: Separates locating one target paper from collecting an unknown-size answer set, making both progressive evidence pursuit and stopping behavior measurable.
coverage_gap: The environment is restricted to computer-science papers in a fixed corpus and does not test live scholarly databases, paywalls, or cross-domain literature.

name: EnterpriseRAG-Bench
summary: Evaluates enterprise-style RAG over a coherent synthetic company corpus containing multiple source types, duplicates, noise, conflicts, and absent information.
scale: Approximately 500,000 coherent synthetic documents across nine enterprise source types and 500 questions in ten diagnostic categories, with a released corpus-generation framework.
measurement_strength: Combines retrieval, reasoning, conflict handling, completeness, source constraints, and not-found behavior over one cross-document enterprise ontology.
coverage_gap: The corpus represents one synthetic English-language company; results do not establish behavior under real permissions, organizational drift, or proprietary data distributions.

name: LiveBrowseComp
summary: Tests deep-search agents on human-authored questions whose answers depend on low-salience facts published shortly before benchmark construction.
scale: 335 human-authored questions based on facts from the preceding 90 days, drawn from six frequently updated sources and filtered to avoid globally salient events.
measurement_strength: Uses closed-book and answer-source-removal diagnostics to distinguish fresh evidence discovery from web-assisted verification of facts already in model parameters.
coverage_gap: The benchmark ages quickly, covers only six source families, and remains limited to short-answer tasks.

name: LoHoSearch
summary: Evaluates long-horizon web search on questions constructed to have large candidate spaces and structurally complex constraint graphs.
scale: 544 human-verified questions across 11 domains, split into 282 tree-structured and 262 graph-structured tasks, generated from a knowledge graph with more than 7 million Wikipedia entities.
measurement_strength: Controls search-space size and structural complexity rather than relying on annotator intuition, while exposing context-management and calibration failures over long searches.
coverage_gap: Questions are Wikipedia-derived and English-only; they do not measure freshness across heterogeneous sites or the authenticity of naturally occurring user needs.

name: EvoBrowseComp
summary: Provides bilingual live-web search questions generated by an automated multi-agent pipeline intended for periodic refresh against evolving knowledge.
scale: 800 complex questions synthesized through live-web traversal: 400 English and 400 Chinese, with encrypted released question and answer files.
measurement_strength: Makes bilingual search evaluation refreshable through an automated synthesis, filtering, and reasoning-graph pipeline rather than a permanently static test set.
coverage_gap: Only one released snapshot is currently available, and automatic synthesis does not establish human authenticity or comparability across regenerated versions.

name: ScholarQuest
summary: Benchmarks iterative academic paper search as intent-conditioned set retrieval over a shared arXiv-scale backend and citation graph.
scale: 1,111 queries from more than 1,000 computer-science topics and four research intents; each answer set contains 5 to 200 arXiv papers, evaluated against a roughly 3-million-paper backend.
measurement_strength: Standardizes iterative literature search with a shared backend, set-valued ground truth, intent slices, and efficiency signals rather than single-paper lookup alone.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is restricted to computer science and arXiv metadata; exhaustive answer sets remain difficult to establish for open literature.

name: SearchAuditBench
summary: Evaluates auditors that localize, attribute, and repair failures in long deep-search trajectories collected from multiple agents and benchmarks.
scale: 1,243 failed trajectories from eight open-weight models on five deep-search benchmarks, averaging 73.1 messages and 65.1K tokens, with expert critical-step, cause, and repair annotations.
measurement_strength: Adds expert-supervised localization, a six-way cause taxonomy, tolerance spans, and executable repair rubrics for diagnosing failures that final-answer scores cannot explain.
coverage_gap: The benchmark samples failed trajectories only and evaluates post-hoc auditing rather than proactive prevention or the original agent's search capability.

name: T²-RAGBench
summary: Evaluates end-to-end retrieval and numerical reasoning over real financial reports containing both text and tables, using context-independent questions.
scale: The current release contains 23,088 question-context-answer triples over 7,318 financial reports from FinQA, first-turn ConvFinQA, and TAT-DQA; the initial paper reported 32,908 before VQAonBD was removed.
measurement_strength: Removes oracle context from mixed text-table financial QA so retrieval quality and downstream numerical reasoning can be measured together and against an oracle upper bound.
coverage_gap: The benchmark is English, static, and finance-only, and its questions are reformulations of existing QA datasets rather than naturally issued retrieval requests.

name: LeakDojo
summary: Provides a configurable diagnostic framework for measuring extraction of private RAG database content across attacks, models, corpora, pipeline choices, and defenses.
scale: The paper benchmarks six existing leakage attacks across 14 LLMs and four datasets (FIQA, SciFact, NFCorpus, and Enron); the current codebase implements seven attack methods.
measurement_strength: Makes RAG knowledge-extraction risk comparable under controlled attack, model, retriever, corpus, and defense configurations instead of reporting one attack on one pipeline.
coverage_gap: The diagnostic targets text-corpus extraction and does not cover permissions, tool or API secrets, cross-tenant access, or production incident impact.
